items.title: Alice MacDougall
items.summary: It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of Alice MacDougall (née Myler), our beloved wife, mother, grandmother, sister and friend on August 21, 2026. Born in Sydney Mines, Nova Scotia, Alice was the daughter of Martin "Mark" Myler and Mary Myler (née Kennedy). The youngest of a large and close-knit family, Alice grew up surrounded by her many brothers, sisters, nieces and nephews. She fondly remembered the many hours she spent babysitting her nieces and nephews—a role that gave an early glimpse of the devoted mother and grandmother she would one day become. She will be lovingly remembered by Joseph, her husband of 62 years, her children, Kathy (Sean) Licata and Paul (Andrea) MacDougall, and her six cherished grandchildren, Nancy (Josh), Pamela, Craig, Colin, Hailey and Tyler. She will also be dearly missed by her sisters-in-law Helen (Ross) Morrison, Hughena (the late John) Quinn, Theresa (Jim) Burton and Michelene (Joe) MacKinnon; her brothers-in-law Hugh "Skippy" (the late Marie) MacDougall, Gordie (Cathy) MacDougall and Lyle "Louie" Pitt; along with many nieces and nephews, extended family and friends. Alice was predeceased by her brothers Alex (Ada) (Gora), Cyril (Duna) and George Myler and her sisters Bridget (Aaron) Beddow, Ann (Tony) Reilly, Catherine (Harry) Cleary, Margaret (Bob) Osborne, Ellen Myler and Yvonne Pitt. Her life took her from Nova Scotia to Quebec, British Columbia and eventually to Ontario, where she built a life filled with family, friendships and countless memories. Family was always at the centre of Alice's world. She was a devoted mother to Kathy and Paul and an immensely proud grandmother. She was involved in her children's sports and school activities and was the mother who was always there—showing up, cheering from the sidelines, lending a hand and making sure her family knew they could count on her. Alice loved being active and enjoyed golf, curling, cross-country skiing and walking.

items.title: Ward 5's First New Police Station in Decades Headlines Natalie Hart's Re-Election Pitch
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, incumbent Ward 5 councillor Natalie Hart is one of the candidates featured in the outlet's ongoing series of profiles ahead of the October 26 municipal election, in which every candidate answers the same questions and their responses are published unedited. The outlet reports the series is meant to help voters get familiar with candidates and encourage higher voter turnout, noting low turnout means a small number of voters end up deciding races for everyone. According to the profile, Hart said she is running for re-election to build on what she describes as Ward 5's first new police station in more than 20 years, delivered since June 2024. Hart told Modern Mississauga Media she also introduced the ward-exclusive Be a Good Neighbour safety and property standards pilot, along with recurring community events including summer ice cream socials, movie nights, winter skating days and town halls on safety and the city budget. The outlet reports Modern Mississauga Media is publishing similar Q&A profiles for candidates across all of Mississauga's wards, with new profiles posted within 72 hours of a candidate's response.

items.title: Mississauga Man Faces 38 Charges After Retail Thefts Spanning Six Regions
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police say a Mississauga man is facing dozens of charges after a string of retail thefts across the Greater Toronto Area and Ontario added up to more than $35,000 in stolen merchandise. The outlet reports investigators launched an operation called Project Bishop in April and linked 38 separate theft-related incidents back to a single offender police described as prolific. INsauga reports victims were identified in Peel, Halton, Durham, York and Niagara regions as well as in Hamilton, with merchandise stolen in each incident ranging from about $50 to more than $4,000. According to the outlet, searches in Mississauga and Welland led officers to recover more than $35,000 worth of stolen goods, including cosmetics and personal accessories. Peel police told INsauga that Anthony Orlando Monteith, 49, of Mississauga, was arrested on June 19 and charged with 24 counts of theft under $5,000 and 14 counts of possession of property obtained by crime. INsauga reports police said they continue to investigate offences where Monteith may be a suspect and anticipate laying further charges.

items.title: Ottawa to Match U.S. Tariffs Dollar-for-Dollar Starting Sept. 8 as Mississauga Hosts Funding Announcement
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, federal, provincial and municipal leaders gathered in Mississauga to unveil a multi-billion-dollar funding initiative for manufacturers, factory workers and small business owners caught up in an escalating trade dispute with the United States. The outlet reports officials announced Canada's plan to match American tariffs dollar-for-dollar starting September 8, after negotiations between the two countries failed earlier in the week. Mississauga.com quotes a minister identified as Khalid saying that if the United States taxes billions of dollars of Canadian goods, Canada will tax billions of dollars right back. According to the outlet, the funding includes $1,000 per employee to help manufacturers retrain workers affected by the tariffs. The outlet reports the counter-tariffs are landing amid an ongoing cost-of-living crisis, with local social services and food banks already seeing record demand. Mississauga.com reports Minister for Small Business and Mississauga-Streetsville MP Rechie Valdez said expanded Employment Insurance rules were designed directly from business feedback to help cushion shifting operational realities.

items.title: Candidates for mayor to square off in Mississauga debate
items.summary: Poverty, housing and food security will be among the issues discussed when Mississauga’s four main mayoral candidates meet on stage for the first major debate of the municipal election campaign in early October. Food Banks Mississauga and the Metamorphosis Network are co-hosting the mayoral debate on Oct. m. at FBM’s warehouse on Eastgate Parkway in the city’s east end. Organizers said the four top polling candidates — currently incumbent Carolyn Parrish, Bonnie Crombie and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla — will be invited to take part in the debate. Participants will be confirmed by Sept. 18. The debate is being held “to ensure that poverty alleviation, including income and housing security, and food security are key platform issues for Mississauga mayoral candidates,” event organizers said in an online description of the upcoming debate. Mayor Carolyn Parrish, at right, and former mayor Bonnie Crombie will debate key Mississauga issues on Oct. 1. items.title: Port Credit Welcomes Craig's Cookies as Chain's First Mississauga Shop Opens Saturday
items.summary: According to INsauga, Craig's Cookies, a Canadian bakery chain known for fresh-baked cookies in unconventional flavours, is opening its first Mississauga location this weekend. The outlet reports the chain was founded by Craig Pike and got its start with a brick-and-mortar shop in Toronto's Parkdale neighbourhood in 2018. INsauga reports the new Port Credit location, at 102 Lakeshore Road east of Elizabeth Street, holds its grand opening on Saturday, August 29, with the first 100 customers receiving a free classic cookie. According to the outlet, the Port Credit store is owned and operated by new franchisee Imtiaz Hussain Bhatti. INsauga reports Bhatti lives in Oakville with his wife, Asma Safdar, and their two children, and the family often visits Port Credit.

items.title: Diesel and Premium Gas Prices Climb Again This Weekend Across the GTA
items.summary: According to INsauga, gas prices are rising across Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton, with the cost of regular, premium and diesel fuel all increasing on Friday and set to climb again on Saturday. The outlet reports premium gasoline rose by three cents on Friday in the Greater Toronto Area and is scheduled to go up another two cents on Saturday. INsauga reports diesel prices rose by one cent on Friday and are set to increase by another cent on Saturday. According to the outlet, the same upward trend is playing out across much of the rest of southern Ontario, not just the GTA. INsauga notes the back-to-back increases mean drivers across the region are facing higher costs at the pump heading into the weekend.
